title: Feature chaining and quarantine orchestration playbook (working)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational playbook for managing "feature chaining" (dependent feature sequences) and cohort quarantines during staged rollouts and A/B experiments. It focuses on cross-functional orchestration: how product, SRE, infra, and data teams coordinate automatic quarantine triggers, isolation logic, and safe rollback patterns when chained features interact in unexpected ways.

Status/context:
- Working draft: meant to capture patterns we've seen in the last 6 experiments and propose repeatable automation.
- Not a substitute for the full release-runbook but intended to plug into the rollout orchestration templates.
- Motivation: recent incidents where a primary canary passed but a downstream paired feature caused behavioral drift in a subset of cohorts (see JIRA-5432).

Key definitions (informal):
- Feature chaining: when enabling feature A creates a dependency path that conditionally activates feature B and/or C in certain cohorts (can be server-side flags, model variants, prompt templates).
- Quarantine: temporary traffic isolation of a cohort/slice to a safe mode (redirect to baseline, reduce sampling rate, or block output) pending manual review or automatic remediation.
- Safety steward: cross-team on-call owner for rollout exposures (rotating role).

High-level goals:
- Detect joint-failure modes from chained features fast (minutes).
- Limit blast radius to smallest possible microcohort.
- Provide clear automation -> human escalation boundaries (when to auto-quarantine vs alert).
- Make rollback/recovery deterministic and traceable.

Roles and responsibilities (cross-functional):
- Product: hypothesis owner, defines success metrics and acceptable failure modes.
- Data/Experimentation: pre-compute cohorts, provide baselines and expected variance, own AB analysis.
- SRE/Platform: implement quarantine/narrowing primitives, ensure telemetry and rollback APIs, own runbook integration.
- Infra/Serving runtime: ensure model fallback variants and deterministic routing are available.
- Safety/Compliance: advise on privacy/regulatory cohorts; own final sign-off for quarantines affecting PII flows.

Pre-flight checklist (before enabling chained feature):
- List all dependent flag combinations and explicit guardrails. (owner: product)
- Confirm fallback model variants exist and are deployable with <2 min cutover. (owner: infra)
- Define primary and secondary signals (latency, error-rate, semantic regression metric, user complaints) and thresholds for auto-quarantine. (owner: data + SRE)
- Reserve a steward on-call window and create communication channel (Slack + incident bridge).
- Create a tiny synthetic traffic profile to exercise chained paths (run for 30–60m).

Quarantine patterns (templates):
1) Silent quarantine (low-impact): reduce exposure to 0% for affected microcohort; keep telemetry only. Use when model output contains unsafe tokens or high semantic drift.
2) Safe degrade (medium-impact): switch cohort to baseline model variant or prompt template; keep traffic flowing. Use for latency regressions or mild quality drop.
3) Progressive quarantine (auto-escalation): first reduce to 25% and run targeted A/B diagnostics, then to 0% if signals persist. Good for noisy metrics where immediate 0% would block analysis.

Automated triggers (examples):
- Absolute thresholds: 5xx rate > 1% for cohort for 5 minutes -> safe degrade.
- Relative regression: model-quality metric (rerank CTR or semantic-similarity loss) deviates > 3 sigma from baseline over rolling 30m -> progressive quarantine.
- Composite rule: (latency p95↑ > 2x AND user-reported error_count > 10) -> silent quarantine + paging.
- Feature-interaction guard: unexpected increase in downstream feature activation (feature B toggle frequency > expected baseline * 4) -> isolate chain and reduce traffic.

Quarantine orchestration flow (operational steps):
1) Detect -> evaluate rule set (automation).
2) If auto-quarantine condition met: apply quarantine pattern (via rollout API), annotate active experiment/traffic slice, and mark incident in tracking system.
3) Triage window (10–30 min): telemetry owner performs quick signal triage (error logs, trace IDs, sample outputs).
4) If human confirms false positive, lift quarantine and annotate root cause. If confirmed regression, escalate per incident severity (hotfix, rollback to baseline, or patch and redeploy).
5) Post-mortem: attach decision log, evidence, and timeline to the experiment artifact.

Feature chaining knobs (operational levers):
- Atomic toggle granularity: allow enabling/disabling child features independently of parent to enable narrow quarantines.
- Conditional routing: route chained requests to a shadow baseline if any guardrail trips.
- Delayed activation windows: for critical chains, use ramped activation with built-in hold windows for automated checks.

Observability and telemetry (minimum set):
- Cohort-level time series: exposure, p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, semantic-drift score, user-reported flags, sample-output links.
- Cross-correlation dashboards: show feature A on/off against feature B activation rates, downstream metric deltas.
- Sampling: store 1% full output samples for affected cohorts with trace IDs and flags for privacy review.

Statistical notes and AB analysis guidance (data):
- For chained features, independence assumptions break — interpret uplift with interaction terms. Use a GLM with interaction coefficients; avoid naive t-tests on marginals.
- Microcohort sample sizes: low-traffic slices may need extended observation windows or combined synthetic stress to draw conclusions.
- Pre-register primary metric and the interaction test in the experiment ticket to prevent post-hoc cherry picking.

Communication playbook (on trigger):
- Automated message to rollout Slack channel with: cohort id, active flags, triggered rule, immediate action taken, link to dashboard and sample outputs.
- Page safety steward for severity >= P2.
- Daily sync for prolonged quarantines (>24h) with stakeholders and legal if necessary.

Runbook snippets (copy/pasteable):
- "To apply safe degrade for cohort X: POST /rollout/api/v1/quarantine {cohort: X, mode: safe_degrade, revert_in: 2h, annotation: '<short reason>' }"
- "To lift quarantine after validation: POST /rollout/api/v1/quarantine/lift {cohort: X, note: '<evidence summary>' }"

Example scenarios (concise):
- Scenario A: Parent change introduces slight hallucination in downstream summarizer for non-US cohorts. Auto-detect semantic drift -> progressive quarantine -> triage -> apply prompt-template fallback for affected microcohort.
- Scenario B: Two independent feature flags together cause a context truncation regression only when both are active. Composite rule triggers immediate silent quarantine for the tiny cohort and pages oncall.

Open questions / TODOs (actionable):
- [ ] Finalize composite-rule thresholds with data team (owner: Priya). Target completion: 2026-03-17.
- [ ] Add synthetic traffic harness into CI for chained feature smoke tests (owner: infra).
- [ ] Update rollout API to attach experiment hashes to quarantine actions for easier back-tracking (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Define privacy-preserving sample capture for PII cohorts (owner: safety).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a lightweight "chain graph" UI in Console that visualizes active parent-child feature dependencies and quick actions (isolate child, force baseline, snapshot).
- Could we leverage model fingerprinting (hashed outputs) to create near-real-time drift detectors cheaper than semantic models? Worth a spike.

Appendix: links referenced in doc:
- Confluence spec for experiment orchestration (link above).
- JIRA-5432: incident notes and timeline.
- PR: console change for quarantine API (link above).

End.
